query: What goal-management practices support high achievement?

per_column.name: goal_outcome_domain
per_column.rationale: Describes the subject-area/outcome the goal targets (revenue, satisfaction, etc.), i.e. WHAT the goal is about, not an aspect of the success-management practice itself. It characterizes the goal's content domain rather than a facet of what makes goal management successful.

per_column.name: improvement_mechanism
per_column.rationale: The mechanism/approach used to drive improvement (training, automation, process redesign) is a constitutive aspect of the practices employed in managing goals toward achievement.

per_column.name: success_enabler_type
per_column.rationale: Directly names a category of enabler (people capability, process design, technology) that contributes to goal success -- an 'aspect of' the success-factor concept. However it overlaps heavily with improvement_mechanism.

per_column.name: timeframe_horizon
per_column.rationale: The time horizon over which a goal is managed is a legitimate structural facet of goal-management practice (long vs short horizon goals), an aspect of how goals are set and pursued.

per_column.name: baseline_reference_included
per_column.rationale: Whether a measurable baseline is defined is a concrete facet of good goal-setting/measurement practice -- an aspect of the management discipline that supports achievement.

per_column.name: stakeholder_focus
per_column.rationale: Identifies whose interests the goal serves (financial, employee, customer). This overlaps strongly with goal_outcome_domain and characterizes the goal's target audience, not a facet of the success-management practice itself.

per_column.name: improvement_multiplicity
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal targets multiple improvements is a structural facet of how the goal is scoped/managed, an aspect of goal-setting practice.

per_column.name: outcome_metric_alignment
per_column.rationale: Whether the outcome is aligned to a defined metric is a core facet of measurement discipline in goal management, an aspect of the success-factor concept.

judge.rationale: Several columns are genuine facets of goal-management practice (measurement discipline via baseline_reference_included and outcome_metric_alignment, scoping via improvement_multiplicity and timeframe_horizon, and enabler/mechanism categories). However mutual exclusivity is weakened by strong redundancy: improvement_mechanism and success_enabler_type largely restate the same 'what drives improvement' axis with overlapping value spaces (training/technology/process appear in both), and goal_outcome_domain vs stakeholder_focus both encode the goal's target domain/audience. Those latter two are also external-predictor/content descriptors of the goal rather than facets of the success-management practice. Exhaustiveness is moderate: measurement and scoping aspects are covered, but key constitutive facets of goal-management success -- ownership/accountability, progress monitoring/review cadence, prioritization, and specificity/clarity of the target -- are not decomposed here, so the concept is only partially covered.
